title: synthetic-workload-fabric-for-upgrade-validation
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build a configurable synthetic workload generator (the 'fabric') that can produce mixed LLM inference traffic patterns for preflight validation of upgrades and LTS/minor rollouts. The fabric will synthesize multi-modal mixes (generation, chat, embeddings, reranking) with controllable distribution over sequence lengths, KV cache hits, streaming vs non-streaming, and burstiness. This enables reproducible smoke/perf/regression runs that mirror production percentiles and exercise kernel selection, batching, and routing fallbacks. The fabric should integrate with our CI test runner, the existing validation orchestrator, and dashboards for pass/fail signal aggregation.
acceptance_criteria:
1) The fabric can run 4 canonical profiles: steady-low-latency, bursty-high-throughput, long-seq-cache-warm, mixed-embeddings-streaming.
2) Each profile emits telemetry compatible with the validation orchestrator (latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, kv_cache_hit_rate, tail-error-count).
3) A perf-regression job using the fabric runs in CI and flags regressions via statistical change detection (Mann-Whitney U or bootstrap CI) with configurable thresholds.
4) Fabric runs produce a deterministic input seed and can replay recorded traces from production.
5) Fabric integrated into the canary stage automatically fails a rollout if latency or error thresholds exceeded for >5 minutes or if throughput drops >20% relative to baseline.
6) Documentation and a short runbook exist describing how to add a new profile and interpret signals.
steps: Design canonical workload profiles and map to production descriptors (with SRE/telemetry) - 2 days
Implement generator core: sequence length distribution, KV cache priming, streaming toggles - 4 days
Add connectors: CI runner job, validation orchestrator hooks, Grafana dashboard panels - 3 days
Integrate statistical regression detector and threshold config - 2 days
Create replay mode to consume anonymized production traces and seed mode for deterministic runs - 2 days
Write docs, runbook, and a demo notebook for QA and PM review - 2 days
progress_updates: 2026-02-28: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, and PM to align on success metrics. Agreed canonical profiles and telemetry fields.
2026-03-02: Prototype of generator core done. Basic sequence-length sampler and kv-priming implemented. Local smoke runs show realistic P50/P95 shapes.
2026-03-05: Hooked generator into validation orchestrator staging pipeline. Observability keys defined: latency_ms_p50,p95,p99; tokens_per_sec; kv_cache_hit_rate; error_rate.
2026-03-08: First CI perf job passing but flagged a regression on kernel scheduling under long-seq profile. Created ENG-62604 to track kernel scheduling investigation.
2026-03-10: Reviewed with PM and SRE. Decided to add bootstrap CI gating (95% CI) in addition to Mann-Whitney U to reduce false positives for noisy workloads.
review_feedback: PM (Sophie Carter): Ensure profiles include mixed-tenant mode to exercise routing/fallback behavior for dedicated/private deployments.
SRE (Jordan Lee): Add kv_cache_hit_rate as a first-class metric; enable warmup schema for long-seq runs to avoid cold-start skew.
Runtime lead (Priya Desai): Generator should support toggling quantization-backed models to test kernel selection paths. Keep API minimal and language-agnostic.
decisions: Use deterministic seed mode for reproducibility in CI and a separate 'noisy' mode for stress tests.
Adopt bootstrap-based confidence intervals for perf regression gating and keep Mann-Whitney U as secondary signal.
Expose a compact JSON profile schema for adding new workload templates; validation orchestrator will accept profile URLs.
Keep security_review_required=false for the generator itself but require review of any replayed production trace ingestion pipeline.
next_steps: Finish kernel-scheduling investigation (ENG-62604) so long-seq profile baseline is stable.
Complete CI pipeline integration and add a nightly perf-regression job that records baselines per LTS channel.
Add mixed-tenant routing profile and test against Dedicated and Private deployment modes.
Prepare a demo run for the next release validation review and include a short video walkthrough for SRE/PM.
